subproblem.title: Orthonormal frames of the same subspace have the same simple n-vector up to sign
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P be orthonormal families with span(range τ) = span(range τ'). Then simpleNVector τ' = simpleNVector τ or simpleNVector τ' = −simpleNVector τ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ τ' : Fin n → Eucl P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Orthonormal ℝ τ' → Submodule.span ℝ (range τ) = Submodule.span ℝ (range τ') → simpleNVector τ' = simpleNVector τ ∨ simpleNVector τ' = -simpleNVector τ
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. (Two orthonormal bases of Q.) Let Q := span(range τ) = span(range τ').
   - An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of Q (Basis.span).
   - It is orthonormal for the inner product of Q, which is the ambient one. Call this orthonormal basis b of Q (Basis.toOrthonormalBasis).
   - In the same way τ' is an orthonormal basis of span(range τ') = Q. Transporting along this equality of submodules gives an orthonormal basis b' of Q with b'_j = τ'_j.
   - In particular dim Q = n.

2. (Change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector on ℝ^P.
   - Its restriction f := α ∘ (inclusion Q ↪ ℝ^P), f(v_1, …, v_n) := α(v_1, …, v_n), is an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q (AlternatingMap.compLinearMap with Q.subtype).
   - By AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, f = f(b)·b.det.
   - Evaluating at b': α(τ') = f(b') = f(b)·b.det(b') = d·α(τ), where d := b.det(b') does not depend on α.
   - Elementary version: τ'_j = Σ_i O_{ij} τ_i with O_{ij} = ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩, because τ'_j ∈ Q and τ is an orthonormal basis of Q. Multilinearity and alternation give α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ), and d = det O.

3. (d = ±1.) b.det(b') is the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix between the orthonormal bases b and b' of Q. That matrix is orthogonal, so d = 1 or d = −1 (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Elementary version: OᵀO = I because τ' is orthonormal, so d² = 1.

4. (Conclusion.)
   - For every α: (simpleNVector τ')(α) = α(τ') = d·α(τ) = (d • simpleNVector τ)(α) (simpleNVector_apply).
   - By extensionality of continuous linear maps, simpleNVector τ' = d • simpleNVector τ. This is simpleNVector τ if d = 1 and −simpleNVector τ if d = −1.
   - For n = 0 both families are empty, Q = 0, d = 1, and both sides are evaluation at the empty tuple. ∎
proof_key_steps: τ and τ' are orthonormal bases of the same n-dimensional subspace Q
restrict α to Q: α(τ') = b.det(b')·α(τ) by AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det
b.det(b') = ±1 since the change of basis between orthonormal bases is orthogonal
extensionality: simpleNVector τ' = ±simpleNVector τ

audit.reason: The common-span orthonormal bases give a determinant factor independent of the covector, and orthogonality makes it ±1. Extensionality proves the stated simpleNVector equality, including n = 0. The pinned determinant lemmas support the argument.

subproblem.title: Mass bound |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X)·C for test forms with Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ C
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, V ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets, X ∈ D_k(U) a current (GeometricCurrentOn U k), η ∈ D^k(U) a test form (TestFormOn U k) and C ∈ ℝ with C > 0, tsupport η ⊆ V and covectorEuclideanNorm(η(x)) ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then ENNReal.ofReal |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X) · ENNReal.ofReal C in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (V : Set (Eucl P)) (η : TestFormOn U k) (C : ℝ), 0 < C → tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) ⊆ V → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x) ≤ C) → ENNReal.ofReal |X η| ≤ X.massOn V * ENNReal.ofReal C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α for a k-covector α; e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).

1. (Homogeneity.) For a ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, |a • α| = |a|·|α|.
   - (a • α)(v) = a·α(v) for every k-tuple v.
   - So each summand (α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_k}))² with I strictly increasing, in the sum under the square root defining covectorEuclideanNorm, is multiplied by a². The other summands are 0.
   - √(a²·s) = |a|·√s for s ≥ 0.

2. (Rescaled forms are admissible.) For s ∈ {1, −1} let η_s := (s·C⁻¹) • η, an element of the submodule TestFormOn U k.
   - Its underlying form is x ↦ s·C⁻¹·η(x), so its support lies in that of η, and tsupport η_s ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ V (tsupport_smul_subset_right).
   - By step 1, |η_s(x)| = C⁻¹·|η(x)| ≤ C⁻¹·C = 1 for every x.
   - Hence η_s ∈ massAdmissibleOn U k V.

3. (Definition of mass.)
   - By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ENNReal.ofReal(X(η_s)) ≤ M_V(X).
   - X.toCurrent is ℝ-linear (map_smul), so X(η_s) = s·C⁻¹·X(η).
   - Choose s := 1 if X(η) ≥ 0 and s := −1 otherwise. Then s·X(η) = |X(η)|, so ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·|X(η)|) ≤ M_V(X).

4. (Undo the scaling.) Since C > 0 and C⁻¹·|X(η)| ≥ 0,
   ENNReal.ofReal|X(η)| = ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·|X(η)|·C) = ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·|X(η)|)·ENNReal.ofReal C   (ENNReal.ofReal_mul)
   ≤ M_V(X)·ENNReal.ofReal C   (multiplication is monotone in [0, ∞]). ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm is absolutely homogeneous: |a·α| = |a|·|α|
±C⁻¹η lies in massAdmissibleOn U k V (tsupport ⊆ V, pointwise norm ≤ 1)
le_massOn and linearity give ofReal(C⁻¹|X(η)|) ≤ M_V(X)
multiply by ofReal C (C > 0)

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree, including arbitrary U and V and C > 0. Absolute homogeneity, admissibility of the signed rescaling, le_massOn and multiplication by ofReal C prove the exact bound, including infinite mass.

subproblem.title: Local summability of integer multiplicities: Θ is locally integrable and overlaps are finite a.e.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (M : ℕ → Set (Eucl P)) (θ : ℕ → Eucl P → ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ r, M r ⊆ U) → (∀ r, NullMeasurableSet (M r) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → (∀ r, ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn (θ r) (M r ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → (∀ r, ∀ x ∈ M r, 1 ≤ θ r x) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * ∫⁻ x in M r ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ r x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∫⁻ x in K, ∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (M r).indicator (fun y => ENNReal.ofReal (θ r y)) x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) < ∞) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)), {r | c r ≠ 0 ∧ x ∈ M r}.Finite
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) and g_r := |c_r|·1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r, so Θ = Σ'_r g_r.

1. (Measurability.) Fix W with CompactlyContainedOpen W U and fix r.
   - closure W is a compact subset of U, so θ_r is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on M_r ∩ closure W, and therefore on M_r ∩ W.
   - W is open, hence measurable, so (H.restrict W).restrict M_r = H.restrict(M_r ∩ W) (Measure.restrict_restrict'). Also M_r is null-measurable for H.restrict W.
   - By aemeasurable_indicator_iff₀, 1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r, and hence g_r, is AEMeasurable for H.restrict W.
   - So is Θ (AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum).

2. (Integral over W.) By lintegral_tsum (using step 1), lintegral_const_mul' (|c_r| < ∞) and lintegral_indicator₀:
   ∫⁻_W Θ dH = Σ'_r |c_r|·∫⁻_W 1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r dH = Σ'_r |c_r|·∫⁻_{M_r ∩ W} ofReal θ_r dH < ∞, by hypothesis.

3. (Conclusion (a).) Let K ⊆ U be compact.
   - ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, so exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure gives an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W ⊆ U and closure W compact, i.e. CompactlyContainedOpen W U.
   - By lintegral_mono_set and step 2, ∫⁻_K Θ dH ≤ ∫⁻_W Θ dH < ∞.

4. (Θ < ∞ a.e. on U.) Let N := {x ∈ U : Θ(x) = ∞}.
   - For x ∈ N, the construction of step 3 with K := {x} gives W_x ⊂⊂ U with x ∈ W_x.
   - By steps 1–2, Θ is AEMeasurable for H.restrict W_x and has finite integral there, so Θ < ∞ H.restrict W_x-a.e. (ae_lt_top').
   - W_x is measurable, so ae_restrict_iff' gives H({y ∈ W_x : Θ(y) = ∞}) = 0, hence H(N ∩ W_x) = 0.
   - W_x is an open neighbourhood of x, so N ∩ W_x ∈ 𝓝[N] x.
   - ℝ^P is second countable, so measure_null_of_locally_null gives H(N) = 0.

5. (Conclusion (b).) Let x ∉ N and F(x) := {r : c_r ≠ 0, x ∈ M_r}.
   - If x ∉ U, then x ∉ M_r for every r (M_r ⊆ U), so F(x) = ∅.
   - If x ∈ U, then Θ(x) < ∞. For r ∈ F(x), |c_r| ≥ 1 (a nonzero integer) and 1_{M_r}(x)·ofReal θ_r(x) = ofReal θ_r(x) ≥ 1, so g_r(x) ≥ 1.
   - If F(x) were infinite, then for every m ∈ ℕ it would contain a finite subset F_m with m elements (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq). Then Θ(x) ≥ Σ_{r∈F_m} g_r(x) ≥ m for every m (ENNReal.sum_le_tsum), contradicting Θ(x) < ∞.
   - Hence F(x) is finite for every x ∉ N. Since H(N) = 0, F(x) is finite for H-a.e. x. ∎

Θ < ∞ a.e. on each W_x, so measure_null_of_locally_null makes {x ∈ U : Θ(x) = ∞} null
each r with c_r ≠ 0 and x ∈ M_r contributes ≥ 1 to Θ(x), so a.e. only finitely many such r

subproblem.title: Termwise integration of a locally M-summable integer series of rectifiable triples
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, (M_r, θ_r, ξ_r) (r ∈ ℕ) triples satisfying IsRectifiableTriple U n, and c_r ∈ ℤ with Σ'_r |c_r|·∫⁻_{M_r ∩ W} ofReal θ_r dH < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U. Then for every ω ∈ D^n(U), writing F_r(x) := 1_{M_r}(x)·(c_r·(θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x)))):
HasSum (r ↦ c_r·tauAction n M_r θ_r ξ_r ω) (∫ Σ'_r F_r(x) dH(x)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (M : ℕ → Set (Eucl P)) (θ : ℕ → Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : ℕ → Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (c : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ r, IsRectifiableTriple U n (M r) (θ r) (ξ r)) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * ∫⁻ x in M r ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ r x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) < ∞) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, HasSum (fun r => (c r : ℝ) * tauAction n (M r) (θ r) (ξ r) ω) (∫ x, ∑' r, (M r).indicator (fun y => (c r : ℝ) * (θ r y * ξ r y ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) y))) x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞); ‖·‖ is the operator norm on n-covectors; s(τ) := simpleNVector τ.

1. (Localization.)
   - K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U (ω ∈ TestFormOn U n).
   - exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure gives an open W ⊇ K with L := closure W compact and L ⊆ U. So CompactlyContainedOpen W U, and A := Σ'_r |c_r|·∫⁻_{M_r ∩ W} ofReal θ_r dH < ∞.
   - ω is continuous (smooth) and vanishes off the compact set K. So there is B ≥ 0 with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B for all x, and ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.

2. (Unit bound.)
   - If τ is orthonormal and α is an n-covector, then |s(τ)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (simpleNVector_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm, ‖τ_i‖ = 1). The same holds for −s(τ).
   - The field orients of the r-th triple says that for H.restrict M_r-a.e. x, ξ_r(x) = ±s(τ) with τ orthonormal.
   - Hence |ξ_r(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B·1_K(x) for H.restrict M_r-a.e. x.

3. (Domination.) θ_r > 0 on M_r and F_r = 0 off M_r. So step 2, transferred by ae_restrict_iff'₀ (M_r is null-measurable), gives for H-a.e. x:
   |F_r(x)| ≤ |c_r|·B·1_{M_r ∩ W}(x)·θ_r(x)   (using K ⊆ W).

4. (Measurability.)
   - For x ∉ L we have x ∉ K, so ω(x) = 0 and ξ_r(x)(ω(x)) = 0. Hence F_r = 1_{M_r ∩ L}·g_r with g_r(x) := c_r·θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x)).
   - On M_r ∩ L:
     • θ_r is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable (L is compact and L ⊆ U);
     • ξ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable, restricted from M_r to M_r ∩ L);
     • ω is continuous;
     • the evaluation (v, α) ↦ v(α), NVector × Covector → ℝ, is continuous (bounded bilinear).
   - Hence x ↦ ξ_r(x)(ω(x)) and g_r are a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict(M_r ∩ L).
   - So F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀; M_r ∩ L is null-measurable).
   - Lean note (checked at this pin): `(isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous : Continuous fun p : NVector (Eucl P) n × Covector (Eucl P) n => p.1 p.2).comp_aestronglyMeasurable (hξ.prodMk hω.aestronglyMeasurable)` gives the measurability of x ↦ ξ x (ω x). The curried ContinuousLinearMap.apply route fails, because no TopologicalSpace instance is found on `NVector (Eucl P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ`.

5. (Summable integrals.)
   - By step 3, lintegral_mono_ae and lintegral_indicator₀: ∫⁻ ‖F_r‖ₑ dH ≤ |c_r|·ofReal B·∫⁻_{M_r ∩ W} ofReal θ_r dH.
   - So Σ'_r ∫⁻ ‖F_r‖ₑ dH ≤ ofReal B·A < ∞ (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left).
   - In particular every F_r is integrable (step 4 plus finite integral), and r ↦ ∫ |F_r| dH is summable.

6. (Termwise integration.) By hasSum_integral_of_summable_integral_norm (or integral_tsum together with step 5):
   HasSum (r ↦ ∫ F_r dH) (∫ Σ'_r F_r dH).

7. (Identification of the terms.) By integral_indicator₀ (M_r null-measurable) and integral_const_mul:
   ∫ F_r dH = ∫_{M_r} c_r·(θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x))) dH = c_r·∫_{M_r} θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x)) dH = c_r·tauAction n M_r θ_r ξ_r ω   (definition of tauAction).
   Substituting into step 6 proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B
|ξ_r(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ a.e. on M_r, since ξ_r = ±simpleNVector of an orthonormal frame
|F_r| ≤ |c_r|·B·1_{M_r∩W}·θ_r, so Σ∫|F_r| ≤ B·A < ∞; F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable
hasSum_integral_of_summable_integral_norm, and ∫F_r = c_r·tauAction(M_r, θ_r, ξ_r)(ω)

audit.reason: Compact localization supplies measurability and an integrable majorant. The orthonormal-frame operator-norm bound yields summable integrals of absolute values. The cited HasSum theorem and null-measurable indicator identity then give exactly the stated unconditional sum.

subproblem.title: Orientations of two rectifiable triples agree up to sign on the overlap of the carriers
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and let (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁) and (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U n. Assume that for H-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ (i.e. H.restrict(M₁ ∩ M₂)-a.e.), every subspace Q that is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₁, θ₁) at x is also a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₂, θ₂) at x. Then for H-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂, ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) or ξ₁(x) = −ξ₂(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M₁ M₂ : Set (Eucl P)) (θ₁ θ₂ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ₁ ξ₂ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M₁ θ₁ ξ₁ → IsRectifiableTriple U n M₂ θ₂ ξ₂ → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M₁ ∩ M₂)), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x Q) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M₁ ∩ M₂)), ξ₁ x = ξ₂ x ∨ ξ₁ x = -ξ₂ x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Let μ := H.restrict(M₁ ∩ M₂) and s(τ) := simpleNVector τ.

1. (Points of the overlap.) M₁ ∩ M₂ is H-null-measurable (field nullMeasurableSet of both triples, NullMeasurableSet.inter). So μ-a.e. x lies in M₁ ∩ M₂ (ae_restrict_mem₀). For such x, x ∈ M₂, so θ₂(x) > 0 (field pos of the second triple); in particular θ₂(x) ≠ 0.

2. (Frames from both orientation conditions.)
   - The field orients of the first triple holds H.restrict M₁-a.e., hence μ-a.e. because M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₁ (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). It gives an orthonormal τ¹ : Fin n → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x (span(range τ¹)) and ξ₁(x) = s(τ¹) or ξ₁(x) = −s(τ¹).
   - Likewise, using M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₂, μ-a.e. there is an orthonormal τ² with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x (span(range τ²)) and ξ₂(x) = ±s(τ²).

3. (Equal spans.)
   - Intersect the μ-a.e. statements of steps 1–2 with the hypothesis (filter_upwards), and fix such an x.
   - The hypothesis with Q := span(range τ¹) shows that span(range τ¹) is also a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₂, θ₂) at x.
   - Since θ₂(x) ≠ 0, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique gives span(range τ¹) = span(range τ²).

4. (Combine the signs.)
   - The sibling frame_sign with τ := τ¹, τ' := τ² gives s(τ²) = ε·s(τ¹) with ε ∈ {1, −1}.
   - Write ξ₁(x) = ε₁·s(τ¹) and ξ₂(x) = ε₂·s(τ²) with ε₁, ε₂ ∈ {1, −1}.
   - Then ξ₂(x) = ε₂ε·s(τ¹), so s(τ¹) = ε₂ε·ξ₂(x) because (ε₂ε)² = 1.
   - Hence ξ₁(x) = ε₁ε₂ε·ξ₂(x) with ε₁ε₂ε ∈ {1, −1}, i.e. ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) or ξ₁(x) = −ξ₂(x). This is an eight-case check using neg_neg. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ has θ₂(x) > 0 and orthonormal frames τ¹, τ² from the two orientation conditions
the hypothesis makes span τ¹ a weighted tangent space of (M₂, θ₂); uniqueness gives span τ¹ = span τ²
frame_sign gives s(τ²) = ±s(τ¹); combining the signs gives ξ₁ = ±ξ₂

audit.reason: The proof correctly transfers both orientation conditions to the restricted overlap measure, obtains θ₂ ≠ 0 from positivity and almost-everywhere membership, applies tangent uniqueness, and combines signs using frame_sign. No openness assumption is needed.

subproblem.title: An integer series of currents with locally summable masses defines a current with the mass bound
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_r ∈ D_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) arbitrary currents (GeometricCurrentOn U n, not necessarily integer multiplicity) and c_r ∈ ℤ such that Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r) < ∞ in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContainedOpen W U). Then there is S ∈ D_n(U) such that for every ω ∈ D^n(U) the series Σ_r c_r T_r(ω) has (unconditional) sum S(ω), i.e. HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω)) (S(ω)), and M_W(S) ≤ Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (c : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W) < ∞) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω, HasSum (fun r => (c r : ℝ) * T r ω) (S ω)) ∧ ∀ W, S.massOn W ≤ ∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation:
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ‖α‖ := the operator norm of α as a continuous alternating map.
- |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal|(c_r : ℝ)|.
- A(W) := Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r) ∈ [0, ∞] for a set W.
- 'mass_bound' is the sibling: ofReal|X(η)| ≤ M_V(X)·ofReal C whenever C > 0, tsupport η ⊆ V and |η(x)| ≤ C for all x.

0. (Auxiliary facts.)
   (a) For every compact K ⊆ U there is W with CompactlyContainedOpen W U and K ⊆ W. Indeed ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, so exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure gives an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W ⊆ U and closure W compact.
   (b) |α| ≤ D·‖α‖ for every n-covector α, where D := √(P^n).
       - For every I : Fin n → Fin P, |α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_n})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖e_{I_i}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; basis vectors have norm 1).
       - The sum defining |α|² has at most P^n nonzero terms.
   (c) For every ω ∈ D^n(U) there is B_ω ≥ 0 with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B_ω for all x: ω is continuous (smooth) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω, on which it is bounded. By (b), |ω(x)| ≤ D·B_ω for all x.
   (d) Multiplying an inequality a ≤ b in [0, ∞] by |c_r| keeps it valid, also when c_r = 0 (both sides become 0) and when b = ∞.

1. (Absolute summability; definition of S(ω).) Fix ω ∈ D^n(U).
   - K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U (definition of TestFormOn). By 0(a) there is W ⊂⊂ U with K ⊆ W, and A(W) < ∞ by hypothesis.
   - Put C := D·B_ω + 1 > 0, so |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x.
   - mass_bound with X := T_r, V := W, η := ω gives ofReal|T_r(ω)| ≤ M_W(T_r)·ofReal C.
   - By 0(d), for every r: ofReal|c_r T_r(ω)| = |c_r|·ofReal|T_r(ω)| ≤ ofReal C·|c_r|·M_W(T_r).
   - Hence Σ'_r ofReal|c_r T_r(ω)| ≤ ofReal C·A(W) < ∞ (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum, ENNReal.tsum_mul_left).
   - Nonnegative reals with finite [0, ∞]-valued sum are summable, so r ↦ |c_r T_r(ω)| is summable. As ℝ is complete, r ↦ c_r T_r(ω) is summable.
   - Define S₀(ω) := Σ'_r c_r T_r(ω). Then:
     • HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω)) (S₀(ω)) (Summable.hasSum);
     • |S₀(ω)| ≤ Σ'_r |c_r T_r(ω)| (norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm);
     • ofReal|S₀(ω)| ≤ Σ'_r ofReal|c_r T_r(ω)| (ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg).

2. (Linearity.) Let ω, η ∈ D^n(U) and a ∈ ℝ.
   - By linearity of each T_r: c_r T_r(ω + η) = c_r T_r(ω) + c_r T_r(η), and c_r T_r(a • ω) = a·(c_r T_r(ω)).
   - HasSum.add and HasSum.mul_left give HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω + η)) (S₀ω + S₀η) and HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(a • ω)) (a·S₀ω).
   - By uniqueness of sums (HasSum.unique together with step 1 for ω + η and a • ω): S₀(ω + η) = S₀ω + S₀η and S₀(a • ω) = a·S₀ω.
   - So S₀ is an ℝ-linear map TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.

3. (Sequential continuity.) Let (ω_q) satisfy TestFormOnConverges ω_q 0.
   - There is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for all q such that, for k = 0, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_q → iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 = 0 uniformly on K.
   - Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_q(x)‖ → 0. Also ω_q(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.
   - Choose W ⊂⊂ U with K ⊆ W (0(a)), so A(W) < ∞.
   - Let ε > 0. For all large q, ‖ω_q(x)‖ ≤ ε/(D + 1) for all x, hence |ω_q(x)| ≤ D·ε/(D + 1) ≤ ε for all x by 0(b).
   - For such q, mass_bound with X := T_r, V := W, η := ω_q, C := ε, together with 0(d), gives ofReal|c_r T_r(ω_q)| ≤ ofReal ε·|c_r|·M_W(T_r).
   - So by step 1, ofReal|S₀(ω_q)| ≤ Σ'_r ofReal|c_r T_r(ω_q)| ≤ ofReal ε·A(W).
   - As A(W) < ∞ and ε > 0 is arbitrary, S₀(ω_q) → 0.
   - Hence S := ⟨S₀, this continuity proof⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with S(ω) = S₀(ω), and step 1 gives HasSum (r ↦ c_r T_r(ω)) (S(ω)) for every ω.

4. (Mass bound.) Let W ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
   - mass_bound with V := W and C := 1 gives ofReal|T_r(ω)| ≤ M_W(T_r).
   - With 0(d) and step 1:
     ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ ofReal|S(ω)| ≤ Σ'_r ofReal|c_r T_r(ω)| = Σ'_r |c_r|·ofReal|T_r(ω)| ≤ Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r).
   - M_W(S) is the supremum of ofReal(S(ω)) over such ω (definition of massOn; sSup_le), so M_W(S) ≤ Σ'_r |c_r|·M_W(T_r). ∎

subproblem.title: An integer series of integer rectifiable triples is represented by one integer rectifiable triple
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. Assume tangent locality in U: for all H-null-measurable M₁, M₂ ⊆ U and all θ₁, θ₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ_i > 0 on M_i and θ_i H-integrable on M_i ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, for H-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ every weighted approximate tangent space Q of (M₁, θ₁) at x is also one of (M₂, θ₂) at x. Let (M_r, θ_r, ξ_r) (r ∈ ℕ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U n with θ_r natural-valued on M_r, and let c_r ∈ ℤ with Σ'_r |c_r|·∫⁻_{M_r ∩ W} ofReal θ_r dH < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U. Then there is a triple (M', θ', ξ') satisfying IsRectifiableTriple U n, with θ' natural-valued on M', such that for every ω ∈ D^n(U):
HasSum (r ↦ c_r·tauAction n M_r θ_r ξ_r ω) (tauAction n M' θ' ξ' ω).

subproblem.natural_proof:
This is steps 5–9 of the supplied proof of Simon 3.13 for M-absolutely convergent series.

Notation:
- I := {r : c_r ≠ 0}; |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞); s(τ) := simpleNVector τ.
- 'null' means H-null; hTL is the tangent-locality hypothesis.
- For x ∈ M_r, θ_r(x) ∈ ℕ and θ_r(x) > 0 (field pos), so θ_r(x) ≥ 1.

Lean note (checked at this pin): instance search finds no PseudoMetrizableSpace, MetrizableSpace or ContinuousAdd on `NVector (Eucl P) n`.
- A local PseudoMetrizableSpace instance compiles:
  `letI u : UniformSpace (NVector (Eucl P) n) := PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace; haveI : (uniformity (NVector (Eucl P) n)).IsCountablyGenerated := @EMetric.instIsCountablyGeneratedUniformity _ PseudoMetricSpace.toPseudoEMetricSpace; exact @UniformSpace.pseudoMetrizableSpace _ u this`
- After that, MetrizableSpace is found by infer_instance, and aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff, StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun and aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae apply to NVector-valued maps.
- The construction below never adds NVector-valued functions. It only glues, restricts, multiplies by real functions (AEStronglyMeasurable.smul) and takes indicators (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀); all of these work as is.

1. (Exceptional null sets.)
   (a) The sibling overlap_finite applies. Its hypotheses are the fields subset, nullMeasurableSet and integrableOn of the triples, θ_r ≥ 1 on M_r, and the summability hypothesis. It gives:
       - Θ := Σ'_r |c_r|·1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r satisfies ∫⁻_K Θ dH < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U;
       - there is a null set N_fin such that F(x) := {r ∈ I : x ∈ M_r} is finite for x ∉ N_fin.
   (b) For each r, the field orients and ae_restrict_iff'₀ (M_r null-measurable) give a null set N_r with the following property: for every x ∈ M_r ∖ N_r there is an orthonormal τ with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_r θ_r x (span(range τ)) and ξ_r(x) = ±s(τ).
   (c) For each r, r', hTL applied to (M_r, θ_r) and (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}) is exactly the locality hypothesis of the sibling orientation_sign. The hypotheses of hTL are the fields subset, nullMeasurableSet, pos and integrableOn of the two triples. orientation_sign then gives a null set N_{r,r'} with ξ_r(x) = ±ξ_{r'}(x) for x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r'}) ∖ N_{r,r'}.
   Let N₀ := toMeasurable H (N_fin ∪ ⋃_r N_r ∪ ⋃_{r,r'} N_{r,r'}). It is a measurable null set containing all of these, because countable unions of null sets are null. Put G := ℝ^P ∖ N₀; G is measurable and H(N₀) = 0.

2. (Union and first index.)
   - M_∪ := ⋃_{r∈I} M_r ⊆ U is null-measurable.
   - For x ∈ M_∪ let r(x) := min{r ∈ I : x ∈ M_r} (Nat.find).
   - For r ∈ I put A_r := M_r ∖ ⋃_{r'∈I, r'<r} M_{r'}, and A_r := ∅ for r ∉ I.
   - Then A_r = {x ∈ M_∪ : r(x) = r}, each A_r is null-measurable (a finite Boolean combination), and M_∪ = ⋃_r A_r.

3. (Reference orientation.)
   - Define ξ̂(x) := ξ_{r(x)}(x) for x ∈ M_∪ and ξ̂(x) := 0 otherwise. On A_r, ξ̂ = ξ_r.
   - ξ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r, hence for H.restrict A_r (A_r ⊆ M_r).
   - Since ξ̂ = ξ_r on the null-measurable set A_r, ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict A_r (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr with ae_restrict_mem₀).
   - By aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff (countable cover M_∪ = ⋃_r A_r), ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_∪.

4. (Signs.) For r ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^P let σ_r(x) := 1 if ξ_r(x) = ξ̂(x), and σ_r(x) := −1 otherwise.
   - Let r ∈ I and x ∈ G ∩ M_r. Then x ∈ M_∪, r(x) ∈ I and x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r(x)}) ∖ N_{r,r(x)}, so ξ_r(x) = ±ξ̂(x) by 1(c).
   - In both cases ξ_r(x) = σ_r(x)·ξ̂(x): if ξ_r(x) ≠ ξ̂(x), then ξ_r(x) = −ξ̂(x) and σ_r(x) = −1.
   - Measurability: for r ∈ I, ξ_r and ξ̂ are a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r (as M_r ⊆ M_∪). Replacing them by strongly measurable versions changes {ξ_r = ξ̂} only by a null set, and the equality set of the versions is measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun). So σ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r.

5. (θ_r is measurable on M_r.)
   - U is σ-compact: an open subset of ℝ^P is a locally compact second-countable space, so IsSigmaCompact U. Explicitly, U = ⋃_j K_j with K_j := {x ∈ U : |x| ≤ j, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/j}, or K_j := closedBall 0 j if U = ℝ^P.
   - So M_r = ⋃_j (M_r ∩ K_j), and θ_r is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M_r ∩ K_j.
   - By aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff, θ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r.

6. (Integer multiplicity θ̂.) Let t_r := 1_{M_r}·(c_r·σ_r·θ_r), so t_r = 0 if r ∉ I, and let θ̂(x) := Σ'_r t_r(x) (a real tsum).
   - Each t_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H (steps 4–5 and aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀).
   - For x ∈ G, t_r(x) = 0 for r ∉ F(x), which is a finite set. So θ̂(x) = Σ_{r∈F(x)} c_r·σ_r(x)·θ_r(x) (tsum_eq_sum) is a finite sum of integers, and θ̂(x) ∈ ℤ.
   - Moreover |θ̂(x)| ≤ Σ_{r∈F(x)} |c_r|·θ_r(x), hence ofReal|θ̂(x)| ≤ Σ_{r∈F(x)} |c_r|·ofReal θ_r(x) ≤ Θ(x) (ENNReal.sum_le_tsum).
   - For x ∈ G, the partial sums Σ_{r<N} t_r(x) equal θ̂(x) once N > max F(x). So they converge to θ̂ H-a.e., and θ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H (aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae).

7. (The new triple.) Define
   M' := {x ∈ M_∪ ∩ G : θ̂(x) ≠ 0},   θ' := 1_{M'}·|θ̂|,   ξ' := 1_{M'}·((θ̂/|θ̂|) • ξ̂).
   For x ∈ M':
   - θ̂(x)/|θ̂(x)| ∈ {1, −1};
   - θ'(x) = |θ̂(x)| = (θ̂(x)).natAbs ∈ ℕ by step 6, and θ'(x) > 0;
   - θ'(x)·ξ'(x) = θ̂(x)·ξ̂(x).

8. (Pointwise identity.) Fix ω ∈ D^n(U) and let F_r(x) := 1_{M_r}(x)·(c_r·(θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x)))), the integrand of the sibling tsum_tau. Let x ∈ G.
   - If x ∉ M_∪: every F_r(x) = 0 (either c_r = 0 or x ∉ M_r), and x ∉ M'. So Σ'_r F_r(x) = 0 = 1_{M'}(x)·θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)).
   - If x ∈ M_∪: F_r(x) = 0 for r ∉ F(x), and F_r(x) = c_r·θ_r(x)·σ_r(x)·ξ̂(x)(ω(x)) for r ∈ F(x) by step 4. Hence Σ'_r F_r(x) = θ̂(x)·ξ̂(x)(ω(x)) (tsum of a finitely supported family, step 6).
     • If θ̂(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ M' and this equals θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)) (step 7).
     • If θ̂(x) = 0, then x ∉ M' and both sides are 0.
   So Σ'_r F_r = 1_{M'}·θ'·ξ'(ω) on G, i.e. H-a.e.

9. (HasSum.)
   - The sibling tsum_tau (same hypotheses) gives HasSum (r ↦ c_r·tauAction n M_r θ_r ξ_r ω) (∫ Σ'_r F_r dH).
   - By step 8 (integral_congr_ae) and integral_indicator₀ (M' is null-measurable, step 10(ii)):
     ∫ Σ'_r F_r dH = ∫_{M'} θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)) dH = tauAction n M' θ' ξ' ω.

10. (Triple conditions for (M', θ', ξ').)
   (i) subset: M' ⊆ M_∪ ⊆ U.
   (ii) nullMeasurableSet: M' = M_∪ ∩ G ∩ {θ̂ ≠ 0}. M_∪ is null-measurable, G is measurable, and {θ̂ ≠ 0} is null-measurable because θ̂ is a.e.-measurable (step 6).
   (iii) countablyRectifiable: M' ⊆ M_∪ = ⋃_r M̃_r with M̃_r := M_r for r ∈ I and M̃_r := ∅ otherwise.
       - Each M̃_r is countably n-rectifiable: field countablyRectifiable, and ∅ via countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero.
       - Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_iUnion and CountablyRectifiable.mono give CountablyRectifiable n M'.
   (iv) pos, and θ' natural-valued on M': step 7.
   (v) integrableOn: let K ⊆ U be compact.
       - θ' is a.e.-strongly measurable (step 6, indicator of the null-measurable M') and θ' ≥ 0.
       - For x ∈ M' (⊆ G), ofReal θ'(x) = ofReal|θ̂(x)| ≤ Θ(x) (step 6).
       - So ∫⁻_{M'∩K} ofReal θ' dH ≤ ∫⁻_K Θ dH < ∞ (step 1(a)), and θ' is integrable on M' ∩ K.
   (vi) aestronglyMeasurable: θ̂/|θ̂| is a.e.-measurable (a quotient of a.e.-measurable real functions), and ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_∪, hence for H.restrict M'. So (θ̂/|θ̂|) • ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M', and so is ξ', which agrees with it on M'.
   (vii) orients:
       - For each r ∈ I apply hTL to (M_r, θ_r) and (M', θ'). Its hypotheses are the fields of the r-th triple together with (i), (ii), (iv), (v).
       - Via ae_restrict_iff'₀ (M_r ∩ M' null-measurable) this gives null sets N'_r such that, for x ∈ (M_r ∩ M') ∖ N'_r, every weighted approximate tangent space of (M_r, θ_r) at x is one of (M', θ') at x.
       - Let x ∈ M' ∖ ⋃_{r∈I} N'_r and r := r(x) ∈ I. Then x ∈ M_r and x ∈ G, so x ∉ N_r.
       - By 1(b) there is an orthonormal τ with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_r θ_r x (span(range τ)) and ξ_r(x) = ±s(τ).
       - As x ∈ (M_r ∩ M') ∖ N'_r, also HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' θ' x (span(range τ)).
       - Finally ξ'(x) = (θ̂(x)/|θ̂(x)|)·ξ̂(x) = ±ξ_r(x) = ±s(τ).
       - Since ⋃_{r∈I} N'_r is null, this holds for H.restrict M'-a.e. x (ae_restrict_iff'₀).
   Hence IsRectifiableTriple U n M' θ' ξ' holds. Together with step 7 (θ' natural-valued on M') and step 9, this proves the theorem. ∎
